source_of_requirements: The owner's brief, decomposed line by line into 26 testable requirements.

items.requirement: Collect a full list of requirements.
items.where: This file; Requirements matrix on verification.html
items.how: The brief was decomposed into 26 discrete, testable items rather than summarised.

items.requirement: Organize and analyze utilizing the full requirements list.
items.how: Every item carries a status, a location and the method used.

items.requirement: Create an executive summary outlining important details.
items.how: One page: the answer, the three breakevens, the risks that would change it, and a 90-day plan.

items.requirement: Anonymize personal information; use placeholders.
items.how: No field exists for a name, address, parcel number, loan or account. Enforced by dataset design, not by redaction.

items.requirement: Personal information must not appear in the final website product.
items.how: Regex scan over every page and data file on each build, plus the structural exclusion in Q04.

items.requirement: Determine the best course of action and decision for the property.
items.how: Four strategies scored on five criteria with published weights, plus nine observable decision triggers.

items.requirement: Diagnose the property as a Jack in the Box NNN with a lease expiring 2030-2035 in central Los Angeles.
items.how: Stated as given. The exact date is treated as unknown and modelled at the 2032 midpoint, with the sensitivity made explicit.

items.requirement: Decide whether to sell before expiry or renew, based on existing economic activity in the area.
items.how: The area's actual activity is documented from BLS, EDD, Census and BEA; the decision turns on it plus the breakevens.

items.requirement: Examine geography as a value factor.
items.how: Jurisdiction and travel time verified; distance-to-centre and trade-area population left blank because they need the address.

items.requirement: Examine income levels in the area.
items.how: Median household income, per capita income, poverty and wages at city and county level, plus total personal income.

items.requirement: Examine school systems.
items.how: Official K-12 enrollment projections verified at county and state level; district and school-level facts left blank because they are address-specific.

items.requirement: Examine population.
items.how: Census V2025 and ACS plus the CA DOF P-2A county projection to 2070.

items.requirement: Examine job growth.
items.how: BLS LAUS and CES plus the EDD county release, with sector detail. The 10-year projection is blank and flagged.

items.requirement: Examine every other factor that could influence the local economy.
items.how: Adds consumer demand, CPI, ECI, three statutory wage floors, capital markets, transfer taxes, Prop 13 and hazard.

items.requirement: Deep research to build a reliable projection system for the area.
items.how: A deterministic engine over official projections and verified rates, with a seeded 20,000-trial simulation. Deliberately not a local econometric forecast, because no official local forecast covering 2030-2035 exists for employment.

items.requirement: Identify the risks of every possible decision.
items.how: 22 risks, each tagged with the strategies it touches, so the exposure matrix is generated rather than asserted.

items.requirement: Identify the best decision for preserving wealth.
items.how: Wealth is measured as 2040 pre-tax nominal wealth on both paths, through one engine, with the difference published.

items.requirement: Identify the best decision for opportunity for growth.
items.how: Growth is one of five scored criteria and is why the extension-then-sell strategy ranks first.

items.requirement: Balance risk factors at a manageable level of risk.
items.how: The tail distribution is published rather than the mean alone: holding wins the mean but carries a materially worse 5th percentile.

items.requirement: Account for business-as-usual events.
items.how: Tenant credit, closure programme, franchisee credit, demographics, wage floors, kitchen-table economics, cap rates, reinvestment, ULA, Prop 13, concentration, execution and data risk.

items.requirement: Account for rare black-swan events that could destroy the local economy, such as wildfires or natural disasters.
items.where: risks.html, 9 SWAN rows; model hazard process
items.how: Earthquake (USGS UCERF3 probabilities), wildfire (Eaton Fire precedent), insurance withdrawal, tenant insolvency, regulatory shock, rate shock, mobility shock, title defect and data-integrity risk.

items.requirement: Use verified official sources for data.
items.how: 21 sources, all tier A (government/regulator) or tier B (SEC filing). Each records the exact text present at access. No tier-C or tier-D source is used for any value.

items.requirement: No manual input from the owner; complete all tasks autonomously.
items.how: No question was put to the owner. Where an owner input is required it is written as a document request, not as a prompt.

items.requirement: Work line by line and verify everything; no hallucinations.
items.how: 16 automated checks plus a recorded verified-text string per source. Where a value could not be confirmed it is blank, and 55 blanks are published with what to obtain.

items.requirement: Review the repository, flag irregularities, provide links for manual review.
items.how: 11 irregularities with severity and owner action, each linked to the evidence.

items.requirement: Create a live GitHub Pages site with a clean dashboard, category subpages, and all entries in easy-to-read tables with a source link on every row.
items.how: Static HTML, no build step at serve time, filterable master table, every verified row carrying a clickable source link. Wired into the repository's existing GitHub Actions verification and Pages deployment.
